FOR E-COMMERCE BRANDS WITH A 3PL

Did your 3PL bill what your contract says, for what you actually shipped?

Enter the rate card from your agreement, the counts from your own WMS and order export, and paste the invoice lines. The checker recomputes every line, ranks the recoverable dollars and names the record that proves each one. It runs privately in your browser and uploads nothing.

Common questions

How do I check a 3PL invoice against my contract?

Take the rate card from your agreement and recompute each line: contract rate times the quantity your own records support. Compare that with the line amount. The quantity is where most money hides, because a 3PL bills from its counts and you can only dispute them with yours: orders shipped from your order export, pallets stored from daily WMS snapshots, returns from your returns log. This checker does the multiplication for every line, flags the ones that differ, and tells you which record to pull for each.

What are the most common 3PL billing errors?

Five come up again and again: a rate above the contract (often a stale rate card), storage billed on peak or opening pallets instead of the average on hand, the same line billed twice, a one-off project or admin fee that appears nowhere in the rate card, and an account minimum billed on top of charges that already reach it. Fuel and handling surcharges applied to the wrong base are a sixth. The checker tests each of these and totals the dollars.

How is storage supposed to be billed, and how do I prove an overcharge?

Most agreements bill storage per pallet or bin per month, on an average or a daily count. If your invoice shows more pallets than your average daily on-hand from the WMS inventory snapshots, the difference times the contract rate is what the invoice overstates. Pull the daily snapshots for the month, average the pallet positions, enter that number, and the checker prices the gap. Check the storage clause first: if your contract bills on a peak or month-start count, the average is the wrong test.

What does an account minimum cover, and when is it billed twice?

An account minimum is a floor: if the month's charges come to less than the minimum, the 3PL bills the shortfall. If the other charges already reach the minimum, nothing more is owed. Billing the full minimum as a separate line on top of charges that already exceed it is double billing. The checker judges the minimum against the corrected charges, so fixing other lines first can change whether a top-up is fair.

Can I send a dispute without being sure the finding is right?

Treat the output as a list of questions with evidence, not a verdict. The generated note asks the 3PL to review each line and send supporting detail or a credit, and offers to share the exports. Before sending, read the matching clause in your contract: a written amendment, a tiered rate, a free-storage window or a different counting rule can legitimately explain a line. Lines the checker could not classify safely are held for review instead of being counted.

Is my invoice or contract uploaded anywhere?

No. The checker runs entirely in your browser; the rate card, counts and invoice lines are never sent anywhere. The share link stores your inputs in the link itself, so anyone you send it to sees those numbers, and the optional usage counter records only which features were used and the day.

Comparing methods? See this checker vs. reviewing 3PL invoices in a spreadsheet.

vs-reviewing-3pl-invoices-in-a-spreadshe.text:
← 3PL Invoice Audit Checker

3PL Invoice Audit Checker vs. reviewing 3PL invoices in a spreadsheet

A spreadsheet confirms that quantity times rate adds up. It rarely tests the quantity against your own WMS snapshots and order export, a duplicate across every row, an account minimum against the corrected charges, a surcharge against the right base, or a charge that is not in the rate card — which is what this free, no-upload checker does on every line.

Where a spreadsheet stops being enough

Most brands that watch their 3PL bill already have a sheet: the invoice lines in one tab, the contract rates in another, a column that multiplies one by the other. That catches a rate that is plainly wrong. The leaks that cost real money sit in the comparison with something outside the sheet, and building each comparison once for one month is easy; rebuilding it correctly every month is where it drifts.

What you are trying to catchA spreadsheet you build yourselfThis checker
A rate above the contract.Works, if the contract column is current and every description is mapped to the right rate by hand.Maps each description to a rate-card fee and computes (billed rate − contract rate) × quantity.
Storage billed on more pallets than you held.Needs the daily WMS snapshots averaged first, then compared with the billed count, then priced.Takes your average on-hand, prices the gap at the contract rate, and names the WMS snapshot as the proving record.
The same line billed twice.Needs a count-if across every row; easy to leave out, and a second identical line looks ordinary on its own.Flags a repeat of description, quantity, rate and amount and treats the whole repeat as recoverable.
A charge that is not in the rate card.Shows up as a blank in the contract column, if anyone looks for blanks.Lists it as recoverable in full, pending a written agreement, with the contract schedule as the proving record.
An account minimum billed on top of charges that already reach it.Adds up correctly, so it passes unless someone remembers to compare the total with the minimum.Judges the minimum against the corrected charges and flags the whole line, or only the excess over the true shortfall.
A fuel or handling surcharge on the wrong base.Needs the right subset of lines summed first, then multiplied by the contracted percent.Tests the surcharge as a percent of the corrected receiving, pick, pack, returns and kitting charges.
A ranked list and a message to send.Sort and write it yourself each month.Ranks lines by dollars, names the record behind each, and writes a dispute note you can edit.

A spreadsheet you trust, with the checks above built in, does the same arithmetic. This checker is the version with the rules already written, nothing to rebuild next month, and the invoice kept in your browser.

This tool needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, the arithmetic runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off. Your invoice is never uploaded.

Common questions

Can't I just check my 3PL invoice in a spreadsheet?

Yes, and a careful spreadsheet catches the arithmetic: quantity times rate, and the total. What a spreadsheet built for one month rarely holds is the logic around it: a duplicate test across every row, a storage count compared with the average of daily WMS snapshots, an account minimum judged against the corrected charges, a surcharge tested as a percent of the right base, and a rule for charges that are not in the rate card. Each is a few formulas, and each has to be rebuilt or re-checked every month.

What does a spreadsheet usually miss on a 3PL invoice?

The checks that depend on a second document. A line can multiply correctly and still be wrong because the quantity is higher than your order export or your inventory snapshots support, or because the rate is last year's. A minimum billed on top of charges that already reach it adds up fine on its own. A duplicate line looks ordinary read alone. These only show when each line is compared with the contract and with your records.

How does the checker decide what is recoverable?

For each line it multiplies the contract rate by the quantity your own records support, then adds up the rate difference, the quantity difference and any arithmetic difference. A repeated line and a charge with no matching fee in the rate card are recoverable in full. A minimum is judged against the corrected total of the other lines, and surcharges against the corrected base. Where you enter no count, the billed quantity is taken as given and the page says so.

Does the checker replace reading the contract?

No. It finds lines worth questioning and names the record that would settle each one. A written amendment, a tiered rate, a free-storage window or a different counting rule can explain a line, so the dispute note asks the 3PL to review and send supporting detail rather than asserting an error. You remain responsible for checking each finding against your agreement before you send anything.

Is my invoice uploaded when I use the checker?

No. Everything runs in your browser and the rate card, counts and invoice lines are never sent anywhere. A spreadsheet kept in a shared drive may be visible to others; the checker's share link, by contrast, holds your inputs in the link itself, so send it only to people who may see them.
